long_biography.plain_text:
The legal market changed in 1977 when the US Supreme Court ruled that lawyers could advertise. Richard David Sackett, already running an agency after an early career in retail advertising, responded by specialising in personal-injury firms. Group Matrix began developing television spots, slogans and media strategies for a profession that had long resisted commercial promotion.

Over the following decades, Sackett expanded the model across broadcast, outdoor and digital media, combining creative production with campaign placement and practice-development advice. He also taught at Loyola University Law School and spoke to trial-lawyer organisations about advertising. Group Matrix continues to serve personal-injury firms, and Sackett remains its founder and chief executive.
long_biography.html:
The legal market changed in 1977 when the US Supreme Court ruled that lawyers could advertise. Richard David Sackett, already running an agency after an early career in retail advertising, responded by specialising in personal-injury firms. Group Matrix began developing television spots, slogans and media strategies for a profession that had long resisted commercial promotion.

Over the following decades, Sackett expanded the model across broadcast, outdoor and digital media, combining creative production with campaign placement and practice-development advice. He also taught at Loyola University Law School and spoke to trial-lawyer organisations about advertising. Group Matrix continues to serve personal-injury firms, and Sackett remains its founder and chief executive.
